reasoning: B wins clearly. It meets almost every rubric point. It requires alpha bleed, replaces the glass card's blur with a darker, more opaque fill, uses an rbxthumb AvatarHeadShot URL, and 9-slices both the ribbon and the slot with SliceScale 0.5. It also pads every sprite cell, uses ScaleType Fit, and exports everything at 2x. A is detailed and mostly correct, but it misses alpha bleed entirely, keeps the glass card light and translucent, scales the slot uniformly instead of slicing it, and exports the glow at 1x.

criteria.note: Keyboard, ribbon, glass card, progress bar and the 'NEW' label are built from UI objects, and glyphs, icons, panel, slot, dots, badge, logo, glow and portraits are images; the avatar uses GetUserThumbnailAsync HeadShot rather than an rbxthumb AvatarHeadShot URL.

The ribbon is a UICorner frame with SquareTR/SquareBL patch frames, which works, but the glass card stays white at BackgroundTransparency 0.9 with the blur simply dropped, not turned into a darker, more opaque fill.
Icons export at 64, portraits at 256, and the logo is split from 1408x512 into two halves, but the Glow is exported at 1x (192), breaking the 2x rule.

criteria.criterion: Sheets grouped by what shows together
criteria.note: HudIcons, PromptsXbox, PromptsPlayStation and PromptsTouch are separate sheets, and portraits, panel, slot, tile and badge are standalone images.
Uses a regular grid with an 8 px gap only between cells (no padding at the sheet edges), defaults to ScaleType Stretch, and its icon and multicolor-glyph colour handling is correct.

The dot tile (Tile, TileSize 24 offset) and panel (Slice, SliceCenter 96-128, SliceScale 0.5) are correct, but the dashed slot is scaled uniformly instead of sliced, and sprites don't use ScaleType Fit.
Never mentions alpha bleed; otherwise every layer gets a destination and the numbers are exact.
Every visual matches the rubric, the 'NEW' label is native, and the avatar uses rbxthumb://type=AvatarHeadShot at 420.
The ribbon is a white 96 px 9-slice tinted with ImageColor3, and the glass card blur becomes a 40,43,56 fill at BackgroundTransparency 0.2.
Everything exports at 2x, including the glow at 360, and the logo is split into two 704x512 images, with a 1024 cap offered as the alternative.

criteria.criterion: Sheets grouped by what shows together
criteria.note: One HUD sheet and three separate device sheets; portraits, 9-slices, the tile and the logo are single images.
Uses a regular grid with a 4 px margin around each piece, gives the offset formula and full tables, sets ScaleType Fit, and exports one-color art white while multicolor art keeps its colours.
Dot tile uses Tile with TileSize 24 in offsets; the panel and slot use Slice with SliceCenter in image pixels and SliceScale 0.5; sprites use Fit.
Alpha bleed is required for all PNGs, the Notes and page background are accounted for, the numbers are exact, and the designer gaps are listed.

strengths: Logo split handled carefully, including the bounds check
Reminds the artist to hide the Note layers
weaknesses: Glass card stays a light translucent fill
No ScaleType Fit for sprites and no edge padding on sheets

strengths: The glass card gets a darker, more opaque fill
Ribbon and slot are 9-sliced with correct SliceScale
Sheets have padding around each piece and use Fit
Explicit list of designer sign-off gaps
weaknesses: The final checklist item about phones drawing the wrong sprite rect is unsubstantiated
Uses the newer BorderStrokePosition property without caveat
